name: Piper J-2 / E-2 Cub
summary: The ancestors of the J-3 Cub: tiny tandem-seat high-wings with 37-40 hp engines, built by Taylor and then Piper in the early 1930s.

wings: High wing braced by a V-strut on each side
fuselage: Fixed tailwheel gear on spindly legs

tellTales: Prewar tandem high-wing on V-struts with a tiny, barely cowled engine
Light, spindly airframe with thin landing gear
Small flat-four sitting out front with its cylinders showing

confusedWith.howToTell: The J-3 is the refined successor with a fuller cowl and cleaner lines; the J-2/E-2 is earlier and plainer with a smaller, more exposed engine.
The PA-11 has a fully enclosed, streamlined engine cowl and later styling; the J-2/E-2 shows more of its small engine and has an older, plainer nose.
The Champ is a postwar design with a smooth fully cowled engine and a more rounded nose; the J-2/E-2 is older and plainer.
The J-4 Cub Coupe has side-by-side seating in a wider cabin; the J-2/E-2 has tandem seats in a narrow fuselage.
